item.title: GenZ Savings Bond for a Stable Future
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
For decades Index-linked saving products are synonymous with safe and stable savings. Still, with the rise of inflation experienced by countries worldwide continuing to be exacerbated at a higher rate thanks to a widespread pandemic, wealth savings have become a core issue for many. Traditionally, saving based financial offerings have been targeted towards retirement or the elderly. In this increasingly advancing ecosystem, more and more people of all ages are beginning to understand the importance of savings. We live in extremely leveraged credit lifestyles, especially the young generation.

“Nations Savings systems are broken, there is nothing left for coming generations to hope for.”

Traditional financial savings products are broken, with negative or near-zero rates, overdue for inevitable remodeling and replacing with a system that will outpace the current rising inflation rates, guaranteeing its users’ savings potential.

Index-Linked Saving Needs a Bottom-Up Revamp

Most countries have index-based or treasury-linked savings offerings catering to their citizens, often tailored for specific demographics, creating a safe way for users to invest. However, bottlenecks with the legacy implementation's heavy reliance on existing banking rails, including bureaucratic red tape, targeted offerings for specific portions of the population, and potential lack of accessibility, make it harder to access some looking for safer ways to store and preserve their wealth. For the billions of people worldwide who do not even have a path to these legacy financial systems, this rings doubly true, as they have no way to protect against hyperinflation and create any resemblance of long term savings.

The impetus for a last resort positive yield available to everyone is greater than ever.

With the increase of internet access worldwide, the most potentially vulnerable populations for savings, the poor and the young must have a chance to start their savings journey early, efficiently, and transparently. As the internet becomes the primary banking mode, the service distribution is cheaper and more accessible. Saving services are becoming more widespread, but how can you create a service meant to reward users fully? This could be implemented on a blockchain-powered network with decentralized finance savings products, realigning the organization’s incentive structure so they do not need to charge users exorbitant fees to remain profitable. Using cryptocurrencies, especially US dollar-pegged stablecoins and other non-volatile assets, any everyday user with internet access will be able to capitalize on new savings possibilities. We have seen money markets like Compound protocol onboard thousands of users from all around the world just with software running on the blockchain.

Flip the ‘Granny Bonds’ Model For "Gen Z" with Smart Contracts.

If we look at how the UK Granny Bonds system used to work, we should begin to realize why a similar system accessible to everyone on the blockchain can provide a considerable benefit worldwide. Granny Bonds are a fixed rate savings bond for UK pensioners, officially known as 65+ Guaranteed Growth Bonds. These bonds, backed directly by the UK government, provide pensioners with the assurance that they will continue to access savings vehicles, allowing their savings to be affected by an increase in inflation even though they are no longer working.

A broken promise with no accountability for those who trusted it with their life savings.

With the widespread adoption of the DeFi ecosystem in recent months, it is evidently clear that the new generation has more trust in technology algorithms where code is law rather than existing inefficient systems. Now is the time for long-term sustainable savings options to become more relevant, specifically to younger generations like Gen Z and the disenfranchised. They can create a nest egg of savings to build a better and brighter future and take back control of their lives.

Instead of being backed by a government, such systems shall be supported by Index Savings products and revenue-generating offerings on the blockchain, keeping the annual percentage yield (APY) well above the yearly inflation rate. We have seen Index-based products getting introduced to crypto space in all shapes and forms, but mostly for yield aggregation and automated investment options for large buyers. Grayscale has pioneered a more centralized Index based product, offering cryptocurrencies alone generated huge adoption, accruing more than USD25 Billion+ in AUM in their Index trust fund, which is more than all DeFi combined value at the moment. The trust is based on existing traditional financial systems.

If we have to have a bond Index powering savings offering that can serve millions of users, then it must be algorithmic and completely automated through smart contracts, offering ultimate censorship resistance and accessibility for anyone from anywhere in the world.

Bringing more structured fixed-income products is vital for people of all ages to gain assured interest continuously. The whole ecosystem grows sustainably, addressing everyday users’ problems. This could be a significant tipping point for millennials and Gen Z, giving them the power to preserve their wealth safely for the long term. With the post coronavirus world highlighting exactly how much the younger generations are left out of the traditional financial systems, an opportunity is being created to empower those who used to be underserved and overlooked.

How would such an Algorithmic Index work, onboarding mainstream users onto DeFi and the crypto savings world?

At BlockSwap Network, we are working to accomplish this via a PoS bonded savings product that will ensure perpetual stable savings for everyday users direct from PoS chain native inflation. Stay tuned; we will be publishing more information on Saver Index and its inner-working in the coming days.

item.title: Proof-of-Stake Optimized Savings
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
Blockchain can facilitate a wide variety of financial transactions securely and automatically that traditionally needed oversight and management of multiple financial institutions. Currently, major Blockchains use Proof-of-Work (PoW) mining methods to keep this ledger protected from attacks and accessible for everyone, which consume massive amounts of energy and only reward giant mining farms with the capital to start a large operation. Using the new Proof-of-Stake (PoS) transaction verification mechanism, normal users can finally partake in protecting the ledger and have full control over their accounts, savings opportunities, and wealth preservation, aspects that haven’t been previously possible within the financial sector.

In the traditional banking system, a system that isn’t even accessible to billions in most of the world because of misaligned incentives, banks have almost full control over a user’s savings account. They dictate the amount of interest you will receive and enforce the minimum amount that needs to remain in the account. Further to that, they perform unfavorable control around your spending, your ability to access your hard-earned money, and even close your account if it is in their interest.

Proof of Stake networks can unlock billions, if (not) trillions of dollars worth of its native coin, and reward them to its regular users directly. Anyone with an internet connection can now gain value through Proof-of-Stake, unlocking a truly open network of value that was not previously available.

How Does Ethereum Proof of Stake Work?

The central concept to understanding PoS is that any user can validate a block transaction by locking a specific amount of its native coin as a security, gaining a reward for this task in its native currency. With Ethereum, a user needs to deposit 32 ETH into the staking contract; in return, the chain will give the user a unique key to become an Ethereum PoS network validator. Once your key is activated, the Ethereum staking software will do all the work for you, and you begin to gain yield from your staked coins. This reward mechanism allows for steady and predictable passive income, creating security for the chain.

With the advances of smart contract capabilities, we can optimize the Proof-of-Stake participation method to offer even more significant benefits to users. The self-autonomous nature of smart contracts can bring this means of financial freedom to everyone, as we have already seen DeFi operate at scale, settling loans and other complex financial instruments autonomously, totaling 100's of billions of dollars in the last year alone. However, it currently serves those with a deep understanding of the cryptocurrency space; we need systems that allow ease of use from crypto and non-crypto users alike to make these benefits accessible to everyday users.

Most traditional financial systems reward those at the top and take advantage of those at the bottom of the hierarchy, but with innovations comes new and more inclusive methods of navigating the world around us. Billions of unbanked finally have a platform that puts them on equal footing with the rest of the world. Proof of Stake networks is an ideal first base in creating a fairer financial ecosystem for everyone.

Advantages for Users with Proof of Stake to Enhance their Savings

Before implementing PoS transaction verification, the only way to validate transactions or ‘mine’ cryptocurrencies was using Proof-of-Work (PoW). PoW mining is a lot more energy-intensive and requires in-depth technical knowledge compared to its PoS counterpart. To have the ability to earn on a PoW network, such as the current Ethereum network, you need highly advanced and expensive specialized computing equipment and large amounts of electrical energy, two obstacles that make it very complicated for a regular user to take part.

With PoS, the verification process barriers have been broken, with users needing to dedicate a certain amount of native tokens, or ‘stake’ in the network, to validate transactions. Besides efficiency and lack of complexity, PoS offers many advantages that aren’t available from other validation mechanisms. PoS allows users to have direct ownership in the network they are validating transactions for, further incentivizing them to keep the network running as they are rewarded for their participation. The larger the platform grows, and the more users who join, the more valuable the validating user’s stake will become.

PoS will fundamentally change ownership flow of assets in the future.

As the younger generations, millennials and Gen Z continue to have more say in society. They will have better opportunities to capitalize on new groundbreaking technologies that create a new financial system ground up. The speed and increased decentralization of PoS will only continue to propel these efforts and adoption while also setting the stage for what the masses can expect.

The entry barrier is negligible to a decent internet connection to stake and acquires ownership in the network; PoS offers something that has never been seen before. The opportunity to onboard a massive number of new users, especially the billions worldwide that do not have access to banking services but have access to the internet, has never been so important before. This technology has the potential to finally perpetuate the idea of financial inclusion in its real sense worldwide, creating services that can be accessed at the same rates for someone depositing $20 or $2 million with no discrimination.

At Blockswap network, we believe that new open and permissionless finance accessibility must be availed to everyday users. And to that extent, we are building a network that connects automated money management and automated money minting process of Proof of Stake chain process in an easy and accessible way that will benefit everyday users. It is a system that protects users’ hard-earned money, allowing it to grow with our Universal Basic Savings platform. We will be releasing more information on this humble effort and its functionalities in the coming days, so stay tuned to keep up to date.

item.title: Universal Basic Savings with DeFi
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
“Earning money is hard, saving is a lot harder”.

This is the fundamental premise the traditional banking infrastructure is built upon. It remains more important than ever, considering most banks are trying to extract as much wealth from their customers as possible. The concept of Universal Basic Income (UBI) is nothing new, dating back to the inception of Sir Thomas Moore’s 16th-century novel, Utopia. A global pandemic drastically changed the job economy landscape, an increasing financial gap between the working and elite class and increasing inflation seen across many countries throughout the world, the topic of UBI has never been more relevant as companies’ technological capacities continue to grow within all business sectors, rendering many jobs obsolete. Many wonder if their jobs will still be available in the future. That is, if their employers are even able to rehire them after the conclusion of pandemic restrictions that have crippled or destroyed many businesses.

Many of the world’s top minds and most successful have called for the eventuality of UBI, with the world’s richest man, Elon Musk, once stating, “I think there is a pretty good chance we end up with Universal Basic Income… due to automation. I am not sure what else one would do. People will have time for more interesting, more complex things. We have to figure how to integrate in the future with advanced A.I., that’s going to be one of the toughest challenges”. Until a UBI based system is figured out by major governments, it is up to entrepreneurs and innovators to create the next new-age systems that can help lift those who are most in need out of a dire situation.

Can Blockchain and UBI Be Combined?

Permissionless blockchain offers many use cases primed to help bank the unbanked and help those systemically exploited or underserved. As a financially inclusive technology, especially with the rapid rise of DeFi applications, new ideas are being implemented that may one day change the world fundamentally. We had already seen an Unconditional Basic Income launch by Circle UBI last year. Governments are still grappling with UBI implementation's basic idea, which gives a broken nature of the traditional system's execution capabilities versus what blockchain can do at scale.

We at BlockSwap Network are currently working on enabling Universal Basic Savings (UBS), a DeFi solution with many similar properties to UBI, but with a mission that empowers the end-user.

UBS allows for creating $avers accounts for its users FIAT money (native currency), with a high yield, USD based universal savings accounts that perpetually guarantee minimum yield for its owners. Meant to be as inclusive as possible, putting the power back into the users' hands, $avers accounts are 100 percent on-chain, have no KYC (know your customer) regulations, are fully self custodial, and accessible to anyone, anywhere in the world with an internet connection.

Enabling anyone to have a savings account from their smartphone.

The current banking system is a massive trust-based network of people and entities who are really hard to trust, as we’ve seen in the past. However, having our money safe is still a basic human need, so how do we know the banking system will be transformed from this trust layer to a technology layer?

Banks are ultimately in the relationship business, they have a relationship with you, and you put your money in the bank, and you trust them, and then there are all kinds of things we tape on top of them to make you trust them like lenders of the last resort and things like the FDIC and so forth.

There are 3 billion people who aren’t in the regular banking system who have online access; the cost per customer is too high relative to the lifetime value per customer, so they’re incompatible with the existing banking system. Still, they demand to be banked and be easily digitized to participate in the modern economy. A population of financial DNA is built from the heart of mobile banking. Sending funds over Venmo, Monzo, Wechat, and Whatsapp, many are familiar with digitalization but constantly trying to find a way to handle their money more transparently. At the end of the day, users want a service that can give them absolute control over their wealth and earnings.

To bring this to reality, we have to have digital money that can’t be seized quickly like cash or censored on a permissionless blockchain. These attributes are perfect for crypto enabled depository accounts, making the technology a natural fit. This is one very particular case of how Blockswap Network is planning to revolutionize the cash set of things, the identity set of things, and the banking set of ideas, concepts that are all interconnected to each other.

So, what does the creation of a perpetual high yield USD based saving account that is accessible anywhere from around the world mean for a global society? It means that soon, anyone with an internet connection will be able to start a life-changing savings account that can never be shut down by a third party or government. It means citizens faced with an inflationary FIAT currency can opt into a crypto-backed system to hold their wealth in USD based savings accounts with an exceptionally high yield safely, almost guaranteeing higher wealth preservation than holding the local currency. This service used only to be accessible to extremely high net worth individuals or influences with connections in more stable foreign countries, but with the implementation of UBS on $avers, anyone can start on their journey to financial emancipation with little less than a dollar - a piggybank for your dreams.

$aver USD account will be fully collateralized and protected without the need for a traditional oversight body like the FDIC, utilizing DeFi and smart contracts that are changing the way people view the powers of blockchain. With the inherent composability and self-enforcement nature of DeFi, it has never been easier in human history for the average, working-class person worldwide to safely preserve their wealth. Blockswap Network hopes to bring as much value as possible to users everywhere with this new, potentially life-changing platform.

More to follow in the coming days on UBS!

item.title: Enabling permanent data availability for DAO Baker with Arweave
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
Enabling DAO Baker data on Arweave

We are excited to announce our integration with Arweave making DAO Baker data history permanently available on the decentralized web3 forever. A huge step forward, ensuring every bit of information related to tokenized baking and Swap Market related dapps transaction history accessible for anyone without any additional cost. Arweave will enable our users and DApp developers to query data for DAO Baker dXTZ and SLOT history and other ecosystem offerings encompassing the Swap Market suite ( Yield Baker, Refills, and Feeder) through their highly reliable and decentralized data storage layer.

We expect this will accelerate onboarding additional DeFi primitives in the future utilizing dXTZ and SLOT products offering across more markets.

DAO Baker is designed with a mission to onboard hundreds of thousands of users on to tezos through tokenized staking with a mainstream grade UX. And to attract all types of traders to engage with tokenized staked XTZ and its associated products on-chain. Thus, Arweave will gain new users and markets on Tezos, addressing their data storage needs permanently.

BlockSwap Network is a mission-oriented firm focused on bringing financial inclusion globally, improving people’s lives in a meaningful way. We believe the best path to achieving this will be as an enabler for permissionless stacks, providing universal access to sovereign wealth creation on top of Proof of Stake Networks. BSN products and services are supported by web3 stacks from the ground up with crypto primitives that protect against asset seizure and censorship resistance. Its services are available almost to anyone from anywhere with an internet connection.

A blockchain built forever meets the Storage layer made forever.

The staked asset is a distinct class of asset for DeFi primitive; unlike in vanilla DeFi protocols where assets get locked on a short term basis, where staked assets are long term capital lent to the base PoS chain for its security and earning a native yield from its consensus validation; that means the data of redemption tokens (dToken & SLOT) are very critical to have longevity and tamperproof storage.

Data history loss suffered by Ripple recently 👇

Crypto trivia nugget of the dayApparently @Ripple lost the genesis block of XRP ledgerIf only they had @ArweaveTeam back in the day to solve data availabilityhttps://t.co/mVACE66Sdz

After significant research into permanent data archival choices, we favored Arweave as an optimum solution that provides data availability for the long-term with greater assurance. Moreover, Arweave ticks all the boxes with a one-time storage fee, indexed storage with GraphQL support, and super fast readability.

1) An oft-overlooked feature of cryptonetworks is that they enable permanent data storage. Why is this so important? I'll explain here 👇

A good thread on the need for permanent data storage for crypto networks and its applications.

Arweave had been running successfully since June 2018 and equipped with great tooling for devs to integrate and use it in a plug and play manner with no additional learning curve. Our Unified Data Availability scheme using Arweave ensures a decentralized source of curated data availability for all Dapps that can leverage DAO Baker and Swap Market functionalities. Any DeFi protocols that would be using Swap Market protocols for lending, borrowing, liquidation, etc have a highly reliable data retrieval system on an API call.

Ok, so why and how is Arweave useful for DAOBaker and Tezos in general?

DAO Baker ecosystem will significantly benefit from Arweave permaweb, enabling dapps to have censorship-resistant font ends that enable anyone to participate in tokenized staking and Swap Market yield sources. We anticipate a lot of aggregation and analytical dashboards will get built on permaweb using profit-sharing tokens, an excellent instrument for the ecosystem to flourish by providing valuable information on onchain financial primitives and get paid for that from anywhere.

Tezos have a predominant focus on governance aspects that needs data to be available for the long term. Arweave is a natural complement to achieving its mission by providing the permaweb for users to interact with all kinds of DApps and its data availability forever. Who knows how the story unfolds? We are excited to see more use cases getting built on Tezos using Arweave storage such as journalism, archival information of onchain registry, legal information of executed contracts, voting, governance decision data, etc. Anything that needs permanence is a winner here for censorship-resistant file storage!

And many more that we don’t even know about yet; let the builders BUIDL with incentives.

The blockchain is in its early adoption stage. Simultaneously, it remains inaccessible to the regular users; the need for more open, free, and equitable systems is more significant than ever in this highly connected world. We see more talent entering into the blockchain; let’s give them a hand to build a brighter future.

Arweave is a novel data storage blockchain protocol enabling a permanent web (the ‘permaweb’), allowing users and developers to truly store data forever for the very first time. These key offerings are made possible by a range of new technologies, including Arweave’s Proof of Access consensus mechanism and the storage endowment feature.

In addition, Arweave provides infrastructure for the creation of profit-sharing tokens and profit-sharing communities, paving the way for a fairer, decentralized web where founders, contributors, and users can obtain incentives and governance rights for their favorite dapps and communities.

item.title: SLOT {in} DEX : DAO Commons
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
SLOT {in} DEX : Ownership Network

“The great thing about fact-based decisions is that they overrule the hierarchy.” — Jeff Bezos

TLDR; We introduce Community Ownership Networks on a fungible token SLOT. The core purpose behind this is to achieve a continuous evolutionary interdependence. SLOT is an economic governance token which can only be earned through participation, and thus guarantees a representation within the governance of the economy. We further discuss the SLOT token underlying economic principles based on peer production. The relationship between Commons and SLOT is then examined to validate the economics and Continuous Price Offering model as a Commons market enabler based on SLOT behavior, which is a combination of network participation (supply) and consensus participation (utility). We highly recommend reading our Stake Economics article to have a good understanding of the process detailed below.

“ After all, democracy itself is in many respects a socially produced resource relying on the leisure time of its citizens as an essential input.” Aristotle

Commons

The notion of a “Commons” is not new. Centuries ago, farmers in England used common land for their livestock. Later, the open-source software movement pioneered this for the digital world. A commons can create value more efficiently than hierarchical government-enforced regulation.

Now, we have public blockchains with decentralized governance at their core with a native cryptocurrency. This will result in wealth transfer with societal impact in orders of a magnitude never seen before. Here, a new type of value creation comes into play with crypto assets replacing shares of stock in a corporation, contributors taking the place of employees, all leading towards decentralized ownership networks.

Blockchain is a multi-faceted feedback network, system-level behavior emerges from token behavior responding to rules and incentives implemented as part of social coordination economics. Tokens represent an individualized state of a blockchain economic system and can be seen as their atomic unit. Tokens, as the atomic unit of state, can make all socio-economic activities trackable.

Commons on a public blockchain will be a resplendent achievement for human collective progress. Nothing since The Levellers movement in 1647 when An Agreement of the People was proposed in England has resembled such a change.

Open-ended Exploration

Proof of Stake network consensus is based on the social coordination of its stakeholders which is an open-ended process for gathering validated information.

Technological discoveries generally build upon elements that were not even on the horizon. For example, vacuum tubes were invented without any intention of their potential use in computation but proved crucial in creating the first computers. The computer only became possible because of unbounded innovation through an open-ended process.

Open-ended systems are a natural habitat for builders & dreamers, where richness and diversity matter more than a convergence of ideas, and a breeding ground for serendipitous inventions that change the world. As Chris Dixon said, most new innovations look like a toy at the beginning.

Social production will do more than alter the production of intellectual property content. It will also help reduce resource disparities between the world’s haves and have-nots, creating a better society under the frameworks of liberal theorists. — Benkler

The Networked Information Economy (NIE) departs from the industrial information economy by improving the efficacy of non-market production. It suggests that the networked environment makes a new modality of organizing production: radically decentralized, collaborative, and non-proprietary; based on sharing resources and outputs among widely distributed, loosely connected individuals who cooperate with each other. Generally referred to as “commons-based peer production.”

“Commons” refers to a particular institutional form of structuring the rights to access, use, and control resources.

The efficiency of “decentralization,” is reflected in achieving an ideal market where each individual acts according to their will. Coherence and efficacy emerge when they signal their intent and plan their behavior in coordination with others through a price system. This kind of social production will increasingly take “market share” away from institutional firms following proprietary models.

Constellations of Ownership Community

The model proposed here is a token (SLOT) that can only be minted through pledging and contributing to Tezos network security and future progress by being a Baker (Staking Validator). Through a true abstraction of the Tezos economic protocol, SLOT token carry a supply cap of a maximum of 1/8 total at any given point and automated minting via a continuous function. The market will have a higher velocity for this issued token and at the same time create a Community Ownership Economy for Baking.

Tezos secures its network with the “stake” deposited by its users through a Validator "Baker". The SLOT is a token that has a value pegged to the total staking balance of a Baker who put up the security deposit for Baking. SLOT tokens reveal the true participation depth of a validator in the network, no individual validator controls it and is held and backed by the network. It follows the exact rules that the Tezos protocol dictates and is tradable on the Swap Market.

Swap Market mimics a spot market for stake assets [dToken& SLOT] and provide an onchian price discovery for buyers and sellers. Under the DAO Baker “Autonomous Community Ownership Network” model, the validator (SLOT owner) will self-identify for a given number of SLOTS (Rolls) they represent. This allows for an increased level of “granularity” when it comes to reward tracking per SLOT and participation at the block level. In Staking Economy, typically users delegate tokens to one or many SLOT's following reward signals.

SLOT: Continuous Price Offering

SLOT prices are based on supply, demand, and utilization relate to its aggregate inventory in the network and the trade dynamics of circulating SLOT.

The exchange of staked assets against other staked assets (or money) is governed by prices that are set to guarantee a market equilibrium where supply equals demand. If prices are adjusted upwards in response to excess demand and downwards in response to excess supply, a plausible market dynamic leads to equilibrium. This process has been named as tatonnement (Walrus).

Tatonnement is broadly defined as follows: if the demand for a good is more than the supply, increase the price of the good, and conversely, decrease the price when the demand is less than the supply.

A continuous version of tatonnement (Arrow, Block & Hurwitz) converges to an equilibrium for markets that satisfies the weak gross substitutes (WGS) property. Meaning increasing the price of one good does not decrease the demand for any other good. Later, the ongoing market model was introduced (Fleischer) in which tatonnement and other price update processes can naturally be viewed as in-market processes. This is very beneficial for implementing a continuous price model for SLOTs based on tatonnement.

Let’s consider Fisher Market principles, a set of n goods and two sets of agents, sellers which bring goods to the market and buyers which bring money to buy goods. In Staking Economy, we assume that there is a distinct SLOT for each user delegation and one SLOT per user delegation. The SLOT owner brings a security deposit of this SLOT to the market; the SLOT owner seeks to sell its SLOT ownership to acquire more security deposit at the price based on on-chain historical performance. Each buyer brings money to the market for buying up this SLOT from the market and can use a utility function that gives an optimal price function to serve demand at a given price.

Value and Velocity of SLOT tokens

If we suppose that for each good, there is an inventory that can meet excess demand and store excess supply. Each SLOT has an inventory of finite supply to cope with fluctuations in demand. It changes prices as needed to ensure its inventory neither overfills nor runs out of security deposit. To impose bounds (elasticity parameters of markets), we use aggregate demand functions for the price changes which ensures that tatonnement converges.

Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) utility functions interpolate between perfect substitutes and perfect complements. Nested Constant Elasticity of Substitution (NCES) is a generalization of CES utility functions (Keller). An intuitive way to describe an NCES utility function of a buyer is to understand it as a utility tree. In the utility tree, each leaf represents good in the market, while each internal branch represents a utility.

Responsive Rebalancing of SLOT tokens

Considering NCES in allowing arbitrary levels of nested utilities, for a price vector with many prices close to equal, the demand becomes very hard to predict. In markets with substitute goods, there may not exist an absolute bound.

Looking at the NCES utility tree of an arbitrary buyer, for each SLOT, three quantities are defined: consolidated price, consolidated utilization, and consolidated demand. The consolidated price of a SLOT is the cost for the buyer to derive one unit of utility from the subtree rooted at that SLOT; the consolidated utilization of a SLOT is the amount of money the buyer spends on the goods in the subtree rooted at that SLOT. The consolidated demand conversely reflects how the delegations in the subtree rooted at that SLOT are preferred as a whole.

A set of staked assets and a set of perfectly divisible goods, each of limited quantity is therefore represented as a fungible token. To have a realistic market setting for a price adjustment mechanism, out of equilibrium trade must be allowed in order to generate demand imbalances which induce price adjustments. For Fisher markets with complementary CES utilities, we bound convergence rates by showing that the function demonstrates a strong sandwiching property.

The fundamentals behind SLOT competitive equilibrium: market-clearing is “built-in”. Each trade carries with it the corresponding buyer and seller on continuously optimized market prices. This allows for “personalized” pricing: staked assets may get sold by a seller to two different buyers at two different prices. In many settings, sellers need not care whom they sell their staked assets to, and buyers may not care whom they buy from; hence, it is “trustless”. And, this is how permissionless markets of competitive equilibrium are usually set up and interpreted.

In Tezos Staking, delegations strongly prefer to be put to work for consensus for their utilities to be monotonically increasing in rewards. Also, every SLOT has a strong preference to be selected for consensus validation rather than another SLOT. This two-sided market has a competitive equilibrium which guarantees every delegation is matched to corresponding SLOT performance.

“If You’re Not at the Table, You’re on the Menu”

Creating behavioral feedback and governance loops that protect and incentivize the people to interact with the new sovereign economy. That is the new social enterprise. That is the new ownership economy.

item.title: SWAP MARKET: {in} it to win it.
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
“A brave new financial world with permissionless leverage and censorship-free universal market access.”

TLDR; We are introducing a continuous market through immutable contracts on staked XTZ for the Staking Economy as the Swap Market. Users get a convenient, easy to use, and simple way to get more returns from their tokenised staked XTZ or a new user gets staked XTZ to participate in the Staking Economy. The Swap Market is based on a constant scoring rule which calculates its buy and sell offer prices. Liquidity providers can deposit tokens to start earning fees. It is very simple to use and to collect fees within the Staking Economy.

During the last decade, smartphones enabled a unique decentralised data gathering model that brought incredible utility to people in the form of individually tailored contextual information through social applications. For example, Uber, Google Maps did something that wasn’t possible before. Open data markets are unique and borderless, enabling a superfluid network of information-driven economies. Currently, financial markets are getting disrupted with increased adoption from crypto assets on public blockchains with their transactions tracked on a token.

Markets are conversations. But conversations only become signal with context. Proof Of Stake networks are contextual state machines operating under participation rules that track user stakes for securing the network. A new financial market will emerge and operate under this new set of wealth coordination. It is recorded and validated cryptographically on a tamper-proof public dataset; enabling a new world of permissionless leverage.

We are exploring this unique database, the user participation at scale, and the economic incentives around the novel process of Staking. The Staking Economy provides contextual information on staked assets by classifying, analysing, and making informed decisions when it comes to staked assets performance in its base chain consensus.

Interestingly, this brings a new normal not just to the competitive Staking landscape but also to DeFi in general where the depth and the value of underlying markets are based on mere speculation. Proof-Of-Stake networks with loyal communities can create high return vertical financial markets based on staked assets through Block Monetisation.

The Promise of DeFi

DeFi is zero to one innovation. It solves non-existent problems to existing solutions. Hence this revolves around a unique audience who don’t have the time, money, or access to existing offerings, thus creating an entirely new network for social value capture.

Blockchains discard the central bookkeeper and allow the network to verify its transactions cryptographically and offer proof of transactions for any anomalous behaviour. Atomic settlements ensure the composability for DeFi protocols to deliver a cascading value capture in a permissionless manner.

We are introducing a continuous market through immutable contracts on staked XTZ for the Staking Economy as the Swap Market.

“A market that never sleeps with unstoppable financial instruments.”

The Swap Market can have multiple frontends where anyone can create a custom user-interface or smart contracts to interact with Swap Market functions without permissions or bias.

Swap Market has three categories of users:

  • Staking Economy: users who swap between Staked XTZ or with other listed tokens and users who buy XTZ for staking.
  • Liquidity providers: users who provide the token reserves used by the Swap Market to facilitate the swap trades. These users earn fees from trades processed for supplied assets.
  • Arbitrageurs: users who seek an arbitrage profit while executing a profitable trade that will help to maintain a price parity of non-XTZ tokens inline with the external market.

Swap between Staked XTZ (Cycle Swap)

The Staking Economy offers various avenues to use dXTZ (delegated XTZ) for compounding returns by leveraging their position in the consensus validation process and associated value accrual. Read more about the fundamentals here.

“This unique swap expedites users ability to earn staking rewards from Day One.”

A delegation token only starts earning rewards after 7 cycles (~21 days) based on participation within consensus activity (block production/endorsement).

Since the rewards are variable, to offer a continuous market the protocol has to decide what a plausible range of rewards would be, and decide what possibilities are reasonable choices to make it a constant; hence this swap has a unique constant trade fee that will address the probability of rewards within a maximum span of 21 days or 7 cycles.

A similar example of this market would be an interest swap between the same currency, using a simple intersection of supply and demand curves within a finite space. Any constant market maker must demonstrate how assets respond to different economic actors, given the context and different information available.

An Automated Market Maker (AMM) for Block Monetisation

Automated market makers are algorithmic agents that provide liquidity in markets based on “sequential shared scoring rule”. In new markets, there may not be enough organic liquidity to support active trade, or the buyers and sellers may have trouble finding one another.

In financial markets, trades are facilitated by market makers who make public bids to buy or to sell and update the price in response to potential trades. However, a protocol with an Automated Market Maker (AMM) can simulate this with a constant formula as an incentive for participation. For example, a recent implementation of AMM by the Uniswap exchange facilitated trades between ETH/ERC20 tokens with sufficient liquidity and also offered token listings with no upfront fees. This enabled regular users to be traders by netting a standard trade fee and allowing profit on arbitrage opportunities, effectively balancing the exchange price.

Current adoptions of AMM widely use the technique called Logarithmic Market Scoring Rules for Modular Combinatorial Information Aggregation by Robin Hanson. Please find his prototype implementation here.

Swap Market also utilises this mechanics under the hood as a reference.

Generally, an automated market maker is as follows: The AMM keeps track of how many shares have been purchased by traders in total for each token transfer: i.e., the number of shares outstanding for each transaction. Let q1 and q2 be the number (“quantity”) of shares outstanding for each of the two outcomes. The market maker also maintains a cost function C(q1,q2) which records how much money traders have collectively spent so far, and depends only on the number of shares outstanding, q1 and q2. For LMSR, the cost function is: C = b * ln(eq1/b+eq2/b)

Block Monetisation:

Do you know what your assets are doing now? Do you know what it is going to do or has done?

On-chain driven contextual auditing creates an adaptable and scalable approach for users to understand their staked asset return at any given point in time accurately, including their past historical activity and relevant relationships at every block level. The high precision of reward accrual forecasted through an algorithmic assessment of the asset’s underlying dynamics within consensus validation activity includes a combination of the asset’s previous block behaviour; their cycle behaviour; their snapshot relationships; and their SLOTS relationships.

You can forecast the future, you can analyse the past, but everything happens in the present.

Staking Economy can enable many use cases for unique financial transactions that are exclusive to its participatory network. The multilayered benefits from an immutable automated market maker are immense. An algorithmic market always stands ready to interact with its users, and adaptively provides liquidity for assets to trade that may be hard to support organically. Dapps can integrate with this AMM and utilise the entire functionality for their unique use cases and jumpstarts initial liquidity.

The Swap Market takes a unique approach for nurturing a new Dapp ecosystem that focuses on the intrinsic value of XTZ moneyness. It enables new business models that take an all-in-approach with a strong propensity for on-chain driven trade and settlement. This includes Dapps that offer substantial capabilities in transaction and liquidity aggregation, asset performance analytics and also sophisticated algorithms that facilitate unique financial instruments such as hedging, insurance, indexes etc. However, these are all based on inherent Dapp composability and value chain fundamentals.

Sourcing On-chain Liquidity

The amount of liquidity under LMSR is a parameter set as a constant and ensuring that liquidity is more of a balancing exercise. This has more to do with finding an equilibrium between too little and too much liquidity which is a driving factor of price fluctuation. On the other hand, accommodating a fixed trade price movement, we need to have a more practical approach for cost per trade as a constant. This could be fulfilled via implementing the regular scoring rule with an additional trade fee (e.g., 30bps) for every trade transaction. This implied cost enables a market maker to potentially run at a profit, assuming a sufficient level of market activity.

Anyone can provide liquidity and increase the market-making depth by depositing relevant assets into the Swap Market. Liquidity Providers are the rational users who are participating in earning an additional return for their supplied assets. This is made possible by the trade fees generated within the Swap Market and is proportional to their share of the market liquidity.

You can trade and provide liquidity at the same time on multiple assets directly from your wallet.

Users can simply connect their wallets (exchange accounts are also supported) with the Swap Market web interface and deposit the listed assets (multiple assets are supported) for enabling liquidity. Voilà … start earning trade fees from the market in just one click!

A universal censorship-free gateway to earning XTZ 24/7

The mission for the Staking Economy is to onboard 100'000s of crypto enthusiasts to the Tezos network and let them enjoy a universal yield directly from a permissionless protocol within a few clicks of a button.

The biggest barrier for achieving mass adoption in any crypto ecosystem is the absence of a frictionless on-ramp. In simple terms, on-ramps and off-ramps are rails that allow users to deposit and withdraw crypto assets into traditional FIAT currency denominations. The Swap Market enables this through pooling liquidity for XTZ/USD Coin pairs simply by connecting a wallet. Dapps can leverage this feature offering a permissionless universal saving on Stablecoin denomination directly from the wallet using Staking Economy and other innovative use cases will bring us closer to unbanking the banked.

Crypto capital markets are designed to unlock potential unstoppable financial instruments that enable permissionless wealth creation in a borderless manner, unlocking creativity, economic growth, and social advancement. We will be releasing further information on the SLOT {in}DEX, stay tuned!

Disclaimer: The above content is published for informational purposes and should not be construed as an investment thesis.

item.title: Stake Economics: {in}finite rainbows
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
Tezos Staking is governed by the Tezos economic protocol which represents participating users in the staking process as a delegate and the only monetary operation that is required for stake participation is delegation. Everything else is secondary!

TLDR; This article introduces stake economics and the mechanics behind the DAO Baker protocol. It is an autonomous, fully permissionless protocol with no owner or administrator, so operations can not be interfered with, altered, or halted in any way. It enables tokenized staked assets as fungible tokens that could be lent out, loaned, wrapped, or traded like any ERC20. It is design to be fully functional with the existing Tezos protocol. We would highly recommend reading our last article to have a good grok on the process detailed below.

Disclaimer: Much of below is for informational purposes and should not be construed as an investment thesis or production ready staking protocol for Tezos.

At the outset, we would like to categorically state that the notion of passive income does not exist in staking and contradicts the fundamental principles behind the Tezos economic protocol for stake participation. Every reward coming out of the protocol is verified against a structured process for fair participation and accountability.

Similarly, staking as a service for a fee is misaligned with the permissionless promise of Tezos staking. These are misnomers that have been professed to build profit seeking businesses around this novel sovereign wealth generation process.

As a consequence, gatekeeping and shadow censorship enable secluded communities to thrive at the expense of the Tezos network and its token-holders. We believe that an interconnected fluid open community structure could be form around on-chain staking for collective economic and social advancement.

Lets extend Liquid Proof of Stake in Tezos to all end users!

The purpose behind DAO Baker is to provide users a mainstream DeFi user experience that is reasonably accessible to anyone without in-depth technical knowledge and earn a censorship-resistant and seizure-free yield from Tezos staking.

DAO Baker is a permissionless “staking market starter kit” that enables staked assets in the network as a fungible token. Validators and their users who use DAO Baker can trade their staked position as tokens directly with other users at a marginal cost.

We modeled two distinct tokens that represent delegated XTZ through DAO Baker that simulate the base protocol staking participation with associated risk metrics and auto-correlation of rewards. It is fair, open, and maintains the sautonomous market dynamics of the stake economics.

Delegate — that’s all you need to do!

  • Zero risk delegations (aka delegation tokens) represent the sum of delegations distributed on multiple SLOTS within a single address.
  • Risk bearing delegations (aka SLOT tokens) represent bond lending as tokens with an additional yield based on a variable token value accrued.

There is no provision for an additional reward or fee for running a validator in the Tezos economic protocol for staking, so neither is there in DAO Baker. The base Tezos protocol calculate staking rewards and dispense based on how validators behave during the protocol validation process.

Sovereign Digital Collective

The Tezos consensus validation process incentivizes participation in staking by rewarding validators for block production and endorsing activities. As a countermeasure against misbehavior, a security deposit of 512 XTZ and 64 XTZ, respectively is frozen from the validator account. The deposit is either released after a preserved cycle [currently 5] or burnt in the case of a proven misbehavior event (aka slashing).

The claim to staking rewards only belongs to the owners of the capital put to work for block production and endorsement.

Block production priority and endorsement slots are carried out by a random selection technique known as follow-the-Satoshi. For each block-height, baking slots are created with an index that determines the priority for block production at that block-height. Additionally, a set of 32 endorsers is selected at random for each block-height. There is no priority list for endorsers.

Staking Time Metrics

Delegation Right: At least 7 cycles (~21 days) is required for the delegation to be qualified for block production and endorsement right

Block: 1-minute interval (time between blocks is at least 1 minute)

Cycle: Every 4096 blocks on the Tezos network with payouts on every end of a cycle (~4096 minutes or 2 days, 20 hours and 16 minutes — ideally)

SLOTS map update: 16 times per cycle or every 256 blocks (~4 hours — same as snapshots). It is necessary to track the assignment of block production and endorsement rights [endorsers_per_block = 32]

Delegations to a SLOT for staking and for bond lending is censorship-free by default and available to anyone with an internet connection.

Delegation Token

A delegation token is minted to represent a tokenized balance of your staked position from a VAULT account.

Delegation tokens are liquid and fungible with 0% counter-party risk

Delegating to a SLOT for staking does not put your asset at risk because the SLOT only gets the rights to represent your XTZ for block production and endorsement activity. It cannot be spent or be utilized for a security deposit that is prone to slashing.

Delegation Token Value: total delegation + sum of cumulative reward from delegation as per the latest block.

SLOT Token

Tezos has only the underlying bond at stake in the case of slashing. At capacity, this can be up to 1/8 of the total staked tokens.

SLOT tokens are scarce but liquid at the same time with a fixed supply cap

Delegation for bond lending is very different. This is similar to the issuance of an unsecured loan or invoice discounting but to a smart contract treasury for a staking security deposit. A bond lender is subject to counter-party risks, possibly losing the whole amount delegated in case of slashing events for each SLOT. Also the Tezos consensus protocol has full access to the lent collateral to enforce penalties in such cases. [block_security_deposit = 512 XTZ, endorsement_security_deposit = 64 XTZ]

Associated liquidation risks are high for SLOT tokens minted for this type of delegation. Therefore it carries different value dynamics to compensate for opportunity cost and to retain the capital at stake. Each SLOT has its own token value which is based on its Net Asset Value (NAV).

Base Value = tokenized balance (total delegation as bond lending to slots + sum of cumulative earned reward from delegation as per latest block)

Market Value = (cumulative sum of delegation as bond lending to slots + sum of rewards earned) + average of {cumulative sum of historical cycle generated returns by slots + (cumulative sum of rewards earned the last cycle by slots x attractor)}.

SLOTS value is based on a dynamically adjusted tracking indicator of the risk market performance that underpins the staking economy through an Index.

SLOT Index

SLOT returns can be forecasted using historical prices and the market efficiency (related to earning, age factor, the share of staking economy). Participation thresholds are modulated depending on the reward economics and security deposits needed. These are taken into consideration to cover the possible offsets in the systematic staking rules. This we call “value accrued on accountable rewards” which may motivate the trading of SLOT tokens for bond lending liquidity. More details coming in the SLOTS Market article.

SLOT tokens are a unique asset belonging to the Staking Economy because it holds tamper-proof historical performance data as its trade value.

In the case where a SLOT suffers from over-delegation, i.e. lack of bond amount, then the validator tops up the bond and readjusts the SLOT Index Ticker to reflect the fallback reserve fund used from treasury accounts with slippage. Accrued rewards for this time period will go to the treasury account and are made available to the market.

DAO Baker is not just a staking validator, it’s a permissionless programmable layer that guarantees censorship resistance and a seizure-free source of yield for the financial dApp ecosystem that can be built to increase the economic bandwidth of the Tezos network.

Staked Assets through DAO Baker will have unique advantages such as:

  1. Absolute network transparency on how your assets were deployed, utilized and earnings accrued. Tamper-proof data derived from Tezos consensus with a block by block accuracy on performance metrics of staked assets within the validation process and rewards accrued.
  2. Value capture through divisible staked positions as fungible tokens open a wide range of possibilities to trade and diversify staked assets increasing returns without compromising collateral and network security.
  3. Anyone can use DAO Baker stake functionality and source of yield for bootstrapping innovative DeFi dapps out of the box with full composability and no gatekeeping. Dapps can better integrate and optimize staking returns and easily diversify it for a variety of non-custodial DeFi applications.

A block producer receives the rewards and all fees paid by the transactions contained in the block except the block rewards are not a constant. It is based on a function of the two variants of block producer’s priority in the list (0or>0) and the number of endorsements received (<2or>24) for every minute.

Crypto native markets have the unique ability to unlock mass wealth creation in a borderless manner, unlocking creativity, economic growth, or social advancement. We will be releasing our first swap market for staked assets in the coming days, stay tuned!

item.title: Staking Economy: {in}visible dance
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
The only thing that happens in the protocol staking process is validation which ensures chain security. Either you get the SLOT and collect the reward or you do not. That’s it.

TLDR; This article introduces the staking management process behind the DAO Baker protocol. NO PROTOCOL CHANGES OR UPGRADES REQUIRED. What will be deployed is a decentralized Staking Economy that runs and operates on a set of smart contracts using a modular stake management approach called SLOTS. This is a continuum of our thesis published on the current state of Tezos staking and dynamics.

Disclaimer: Much of the below is for informational purposes and should not be construed as an investment thesis or production-ready staking protocol for Tezos.

The major driver for user participation on the Tezos blockchain is its permissionless staking process and ad-hoc services. In recent months, the degree of decentralization on participation has shrunk as centralized exchanges and other crypto institutions have stepped in aggressively with huge subsidized near zero fee rates on rewards generated. Moreover, they placed an iron curtain on user participation and further usage of the token (XTZ) that delegated to them for staking. Essentially providing staking services has become a race to the bottom, with many validators in Tezos forced to negotiate off-chain contracts to maintain their bond capacity.

Independent PoS staking validators have proposed different mechanisms to maintain user retention and protect their business from large staking providers. These range from classic derivative instruments to liquid staking or other more complicated approaches such as diversifying staked assets for Decentralized Financial (DeFi) primitives. Yet, we did not see a simple, effective on-chain staking validator proposal emerging on the Tezos protocol.

Tezos staking is complicated due to the complex off-chain and on-chain interaction of staking participants, coupled with the discretionary staking rewards distribution rights held by staking validators.

A proposed solution to this problem is programmable staking supporting any kind of stake distribution defined by the validator who deploys the contract; however, protocol changes are required and have unintended consequences.

Staking Economy

DAO Baker architecture discards the concept of a single entity as a validator entirely for an on-chain smart contract. Therefore, staking validators no longer specify the reward rate nor control the reward distribution when accepting delegation. Instead, users merely delegate the funds to a staking SLOT address, and DAO Baker automates the rest, including in-protocol reward distribution. Users receive a fungible token for the supplied asset as a tokenized stake representation so that the user can withdraw the asset at any time by burning the token.

DAO Baker enables a fully permissionless on-chain staking economy that allows anyone who has XTZ to earn rewards directly from the Tezos protocol consensus staking activity securely and transparently.

The whole process takes place on-chain. Hence, this is a very simple but very different from the traditional staking validator that we are used to:

Key Components of Stake Management:👇

  1. Account Management( VAULT)
  • Delegation Account
  • Bond Lender Account

2. Stake Management (SLOT)

  • SLOT ID
  • SLOT Ownership and Representation

3. Tokenised Stake Position (FAUCET)

  • Token Factory
  • Token Standard FA1.2 (ERC20 compatible)

VAULT: Account Management

The current design of the protocol supports delegations from VAULT via SLOTS for staking. VAULT allows the implementation of any custom logic in how funds are delegated, collected, redistributed, tokenized within the system. VAULT is an on-chain smart account management system that has composability with DeFi Dapps.

Users can make deposits and stake XTZ by simply sending XTZ to the contract, and the contract will automate the account generation and rewards allocation to that address. Account addresses are counterfactual based on the initial user deposit key and can be deployed safe by anyone using VAULT. A user can make withdrawals partially or wholly. When withdrawn altogether, the user automatically redeems and transfers the account balance XTZ to the originated address. A user may cancel a delegation should they wish to withdraw their balance with accumulated rewards.

There is also an account recovery option built-in; “Escape Hatch.” This can be used in the event if a user has lost access to their account, or the contract has been compromised. Additional features will be rolled out in phases for VAULT, such as the ability to program custom payouts and portfolio management features with role-based access control for dApps.

VAULT maximizes the potential of a staking market with transparently adjusted price risks on participation. These fall under two categories: risk tokens vs zero risk tokens, which yield independent inflationary rewards and returns that are adjusted dynamically for optimal returns and market equilibrium.

dToken — Delegations are zero risk tokens where users earn rewards from participating in the consensus process by delegating their XTZ to the desired validator address.

SLOT tokens are risk tokens where it covers the cost of security deposits (bond amount) running a validator, and 100% slashable by the Tezos Protocol for a slashing event.

SLOTS: Stake Management

SLOTS effectively simulates the Tezos protocol consensus validation reward structure within the validator asset allocation to maintain parity on reward distribution inline with its performance. SLOTS acts as a way of assembling batches for asset flow within the staking market. Records of the state of SLOTS distribution map updates every 256 blocks.

SLOTS keep a permanent record of every batch that ever took place to determine “who sent what to who”, and how their account balances have changed. The result of this process is recorded as an on-chain commit hash of what happened on the stake distribution network.

SLOTS are batches of delegations with an ID on the blockchain, and the delegations are users lending token balances from one address to another.

Tezos has only the underlying bond at stake in case of slashing. At capacity, this will be up to 1/8 of the total staked tokens. This is the base requirement to become a SLOT owner who will supply the bond collateral to sponsor a SLOT. However, it is recommended to keep an excess on the lending account as a collateralized buffer to protect rewards from any undue redelegations.

We implement the arbitrary concept of baking SLOTS for modular stake management in line with the core protocol. SLOT represents a set of XTZ delegated to a SLOT ID (key) ensured by a bond lender, aka SLOT Owner. SLOTS hold 8,000 XTZ, the same as a ROLL in the core consensus staking process; SLOTS are an abstraction of a ROLL in the Tezos core protocol.

BAKING SLOTS

Each SLOT owner has a stack of SLOTS (SLOT ID) plus an “excess,” which is always an amount smaller than 8000 XTZ. When tokens are moved from one SLOT to the other, the excess is used. If it is not enough, the SLOT needs to be “refilled,” meaning the delegated token will move from the existing group of SLOTS to open SLOTS belonging to the validator. This is done until the amount is covered, and some excess possibly remains. When the other SLOT is credited, the amount is added to the “excess.” If it becomes greater than the SLOT requirement, the SLOT is removed from the open SLOTS and allocated to the SLOT owner. If the open SLOTS are empty, a new SLOT is created. This preserves the property that if the SLOT is changed through several transactions, the SLOT assignment is preserved, even if each operation moves less than a full SLOT.

The advantage of tracking delegations in this way is that a SLOT owner creating a stake manipulation cannot easily change the SLOTS assigned to them, even if they control the underlying delegations and shuffle them around.

SLOT owners can mitigate the risk of losing rewards by leaning on fund sources to provide an overdraft mechanism to meet the refill requirement for a preserved cycle period. Stake Economics will be elaborated later in detail.

FAUCET: Tokenised Stake Position

The staking market should support multiple SLOT owners by using a SLOT token to track each SLOT share of the market. The FAUCET allows anyone to mint a custom SLOT token. Similarly, a token will be issued for a deposited user’s stake. The tokens have the right to withdraw the underlying balance and rewards. This provides staking liquidity and allows staked tokens to be traded.

Zero risk delegations (aka delegation tokens) can represent the sum of delegations distributed on multiple SLOTS within a single address.

Risk bearing delegations (aka SLOT tokens) for bond lenders are tokens with an added earning and a variable token value subject to the delegations represented.

Delegation Token: Tokenised balance of delegation

Sum of delegated XTZ + Rewards earned

SLOT Token: The tokenized value of SLOTS

(Sum of SLOT balances + Rewards collected from Protocol) x SLOTS efficiency

SLOT tokens can be associated with multiple SLOTS as long as it shares the same owner address or VAULT address.

Each SLOT has its token value, which is based on its Net Asset Value (NAV). SLOTS value is based on a dynamically adjusted tracking indicator of the risk market underpinning the staking economy.

When you have something at stake, there is always an inherent risk but usually opportunity for reward; even if there is an assumption of zero risk scenarios.

Stake Economics will be covered in future articles; stay tuned!

Keep an eye on further implementation details that will roll out in phases in the coming weeks. We would be grateful to have feedback from the community. The DAO Baker protocol is a 100% open source project and a common good.

** update made on a sentence that referred to DAO Baker borrowing as a bond lender, and thanks to the community member for pointing it out.

item.title: Bakers Are Not Protocol Politicians
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
“We propose a unique way of achieving maximum representation within the Tezos community by embodying a role for a Protocol Politician in the governance process without any protocol change.”

Satoshi Nakamoto was (is) the figurehead Protocol Politician. He made cryptocurrency a reality through Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System.

TLDR: DAO Baker (an automated baking management system) focusing here on the governance element that enables a zero barrier participation layer and ensures voices from every corner of the Tezos community are registered and heard keeping its augustness. The mission is to make Tezos staking (aka baking) more decentralised with minimal interference from external discretionary entities. If you haven’t read the piece on automated monetary management for baking, we highly recommend reading our previous article.

Tezos as the Digital Commonwealth
Tezos is a self-amending blockchain network with a social contract that incorporates a formal, on-chain governance mechanism for proposing, selecting, testing, and activating protocol upgrades without the need to hard fork. You can read more about the Tezos governance process from this overview by Jacob Arluck.

Bakers Role in Governance
The inflationary reward from Tezos chain validation is a zero-sum redistribution mechanism. It is designed to incentivise token holders to put their tokens to work and secure the network as covered in our last article.

However, on-chain governance is a novel process that evokes potentially transformative notions of user empowerment by deciding how the base protocol must be maintained. In due course, it will self-amend for its continuous guarantee of users interest. Therefore it requires maximum participation across the board collecting feedback from diverse groups it represents.

Current Baker dominated governance process is an ambiguous and shallow practice. There is a risk that Bakers are reduced in practice to limited forms of user deliberation on staking rewards and service fees that rely on simplistic theories of passive income.

As a corollary, existing participation layers are highly inefficient by lacking any meaningful discourse and engagement on a grassroots level with votes being delegated to Bakers by default.

Governance on the Tezos network is primarily carried out by staking entities (aka Bakers), as maintainers of the network. Bakers are also the voters in a Tezos formal upgrade process with their votes proportional to the size of their stake (including delegations).

If you need to cast your vote, you need to be a Baker on the Tezos network which requires a minimum of 1 roll, 8000 XTZ or approx 10,000–15,000 USD at time of publishing. This is a large amount for almost 90% of the world’s population especially considering this an experimental process. Hence, the concentration of votes is held within the hands of a few Bakers who manage a large balance in staking. Compared to the ratio of votes held by small Bakers, this is greatly disproportionate.

Enter the Protocol Politician
Tezos has a continuum governance process by keeping a three month recurring cycle for the amendment process. This gives sufficient time for discourse at various levels on a variety of subjects and proposals which can escalate the urgency if necessary for a user-friendly engagement model. The same way our well-functioning democratic societies conduct civil discourse addressing community needs.

Accountability, Transparency, Participation, and Inclusion

We devised the Protocol Politician role for an effective decentralised representation and efficient capturing of the whole discourse sentiment from a diverse set of stakeholders who have skin in the game. The process focuses on the user with greater attention to accountability and participation to minimize the distance between the XTZ hodler and active protocol participant. This results in engagement on multiple levels empowering the pursuit of financial freedom that guarantees a better socioeconomic outcome.

We require more diversity and freedom of expression in this new socioeconomic experiment by providing unbiased, permissionless engagement for anyone universally.

Protocol Politicians only need to deposit 8 % of the bond amount of a roll to register and seek delegation via the DAO Baker contract.

Social Accountability
1) Anyone could register as a Protocol Politician by publishing a charter/proposal (a simple description to communicate with the Tezos community) to seek delegation.

2) A Protocol Politician needs to receive delegations for one complete roll to qualify for baking rights.

3) Upon receiving successful delegations, the Protocol Politician (an individual or a group) with a pseudonymous name of their choosing will then be assigned with a Baker key address by DAO Baker.

“Pseudonymity is freedom after the speech”
— Yakov Smirnoff

Pseudonymity provides accountability and acts as an effective shield from character assassination, so the person can walk unscathed regardless of ideals, opinions and proposal he/she/they submit for enactment.

Sovereign Collectives can be an effective tool for bargaining and lobbying to enforce the will of the community on protocol amendments and act as the first-line defence against any hostile takeover. We have seen a few examples of exchange interference on governance on PoS protocols (EOS, Steemit). This is an active threat looming over Tezos especially since it holds more than $1 Billion USD in asset value with a thriving community.

We highly recommend listening to the recent Nic Carter podcast discussing with Balaji Srinivasan on the broader prospects of Sovereign Collective within a Digital Commonwealth and its potential impact on society.

Currently, Bakers collectively stake more than 80,000 rolls on the Tezos network. If we consider a scenario with a minimum of 20,000 Protocol Politicians with 25% representation on the total number of rolls (1 roll = 1 Protocol Politician) this would have a sweeping impact in the governance process.

Governance Participation
We are moving towards community relationship managers to come to existence like how social media managers operate for every business out there. Protocol Politicians could be serving key industry segments (games, Defi, STO) representing their Dapps.

We will be releasing the codebase and comprehensive implementation details for the governance model in the coming weeks. We would be grateful to have feedback from the community and incorporate those in our feature rollout. DAO Baker is a 100% open source project as a common good.

Bakers Are Not Protocol Politicians was originally published in Blockswap Network Blog on Medium, where people are continuing the conversation by highlighting and responding to this story.

item.title: DAO Baker — DAO for $2 Billion at Stake
item.dc:creator: Blockswap
item.content:encoded:
DAO Baker — DAO for $2 Billion at Stake

DAO Baker is an earnest effort to decentralise Tezos (XTZ) staking (aka baking) through a set of self-enforcing smart contracts that will provide block by block transparency and auditability, thus minimising reliance on external discretionary entities.

The project is 100% open source and currently a proof of concept (do not deploy). You may access source code on Github here and see the deployed contract on TzStats. It currently works on Babylon but will be tested on Carthage in the coming weeks.

The purpose is to address the user experience and inefficiency plaguing the current baking process that limits mainstream non-technical crypto user participation within Tezos. Smart contract based baking would be able to process programmable monetary management of the entire process whilst also be fully auditable on-chain.

“DAO Baker envisions helping crypto enthusiasts enjoy a universal yield direct from a permissionless protocol with just a few clicks of a button.”

What’s at Stake Now?
Staking (aka Baking in Tezos) is similar to depositing funds into a bank account and receiving an interest based on an annual interest rate. The higher your deposit is, the higher the amount you receive. This looks very similar to interest income but for more details, check out this article. What is important to remember is that staking rewards are calculated by the protocol but distributed by the baking services based on how validators behave during the protocol validation process in its entirety.

Cartelisation of Baking Services
Tezos (XTZ) is the most successful PoS chain out there with a novel on-chain governance process with almost 80% participation rate on staking. We should consider 2 Billion USD has been staked by crypto enthusiasts for securing the chain which is a testament to the confidence in Tezos. However, the existing landscape of staking is highly centralised and alarming to the social contract.

Tezos staking is thriving, with over 78% of all tokens staked. However, exchanges are eating away at returns with outrageous fees.

Major Factors
Tezos staking is largely driven by egalitarianism and enthusiasts, but the technical experience needed alongside operating costs make it difficult for small bakers to triumph over large bakers. Eventually, many have been forced to curb their enthusiasm and close down their services. You can see the number of abandoned XTZ validator services in the Graveyard section of MyTezosBaker.

Proposal
DAO Baker wants to reduce these uncertainties and give users a more transparent way to take part in this novel process of wealth creation by securing the Tezos protocol with block by block visibility of reward generation and distribution.

We live in a world where you press a button; you get your taxi, your food is delivered to your doorstep, all with live tracking. There is no reason we shouldn’t have better visibility for our hard-earned wealth that is put to work on a permissionless immutable ledger. This is the basic assurance that blockchain guarantees to anyone universally.

Our first component of the automated contract-driven baking process is out there and you can experiment (do not deploy). We will be releasing more features in the coming weeks and your valuable feedback is vital to making this protocol live and accessible for anyone.

Here are a few features we want to work on:

  • Publicly auditable tamper-proof monetary management of the process
  • Packaged technical infrastructure ensuring automated deployment of the validation process
  • Validators scoring index for efficiency and behaviour (green, orange, red)
  • Deploying advanced instruments for mass participation using decentralised financial primitives
